claims.feature: register borrowed from a native genre
claims.claim: The Ding et al. Chinese version sounds like traditional wuxia fiction, while Chu produced a more popular version.
claims.source: Translating The Lord of the Rings (Wikipedia)

claims.claim: Parcerisas deliberately larded his Catalan Hobbit with learned or slightly archaic forms for school readers, gave the southern Men (Boromir, Faramir) dialect traits, and made the orcs' speech as broken as possible.
claims.source: Francesc Parcerisas, 'Traduir J. R. R. Tolkien' (Traducció literària, URV 2018)

claims.claim: Parcerisas notes the German case is the inverse of the Swedish: the first (Carroux) enjoys more prestige than the 2000 retranslation.
claims.source: Francesc Parcerisas, 'Traduir J. R. R. Tolkien' (Traducció literària, URV 2018)

claims.claim: Ohlmarks shifted Tolkien's simple language into hyperbolic, high-faluting expressions, adding words and long paraphrases throughout.
claims.source: Translation of The Lord of the Rings into Swedish (Wikipedia)

claims.claim: Ohlmarks claimed he had produced an interpretation of Tolkien, not a straight translation, and refused revision.
claims.source: Translation of The Lord of the Rings into Swedish (Wikipedia)
claims.quote: an interpretation of Tolkien, not a straight translation

claims.claim: Andersson's prose matched Tolkien's laconic tone, using 24 words where Ohlmarks used 42 in one sampled sentence.
claims.source: Translation of The Lord of the Rings into Swedish (Wikipedia)

claims.claim: Critics of the 2005 version called it readable, even and largely correct, with prose following the original's fluent style very closely.
claims.source: Translation of The Lord of the Rings into Swedish (Wikipedia)
claims.quote: readable, even and in large part correct

claims.claim: Ohlmarks's interpretive names include Vattnadal (confusing 'riven' with 'river'), Lavskägge (reading 'beam' as light) and Björnavad (from 'Bruin').
claims.source: Translation of The Lord of the Rings into Swedish (Wikipedia)

claims.claim: Tolkien found Ohlmarks a conceited person and his version even worse than the Dutch, and called the nine-page list of altered names both puzzling and irritating.
claims.source: Translation of The Lord of the Rings into Swedish (Wikipedia)

claims.claim: One reviewer conceded Ohlmarks's 'Vidstige' even outdoes the original's 'Strider'.
claims.source: Translation of The Lord of the Rings into Swedish (Wikipedia)

claims.claim: Tolkien's Guide to the Names was produced in response to Ohlmarks, and Ohlmarks later turned hostile, publishing Tolkien and Black Magic in 1982.
Andreas Brunner (2004) wrote that Ohlmarks added adjectives and spruced up dialogue, producing a delightful but quite different book.
claims.source: Översättning av Sagan om ringen till svenska (sv.wikipedia)

claims.claim: Leif Jacobsen documented padding such as 'six meals a day' becoming 'sex vällagade måltider om dagen'.
claims.source: Översättning av Sagan om ringen till svenska (sv.wikipedia)

claims.claim: Ohlmarks stated in 1978 that he rewrote after a plain draft to make the world feel ancient and distant from England.
claims.source: Översättning av Sagan om ringen till svenska (sv.wikipedia)

claims.claim: Malte Persson found the Ohlmarks text packed with misunderstandings, misreadings, inconsistencies and arbitrary additions, including Merry credited with the Witch-king's death-blow and two names for the Prancing Pony.
claims.source: Översättning av Sagan om ringen till svenska (sv.wikipedia)

verdicts.trueWording: "sound like a traditional Chinese wuxia [martial arts fiction] story"
verdicts.note: Raw wikitext of en.wikipedia Translating_The_Lord_of_the_Rings, Chinese section, reached via action=raw. Page: "Li states that Ding et al's version may be more literary, at the cost of making it 'sound like a traditional Chinese wuxia [martial arts fiction] story'. In contrast, Chu, more familiar with Western fantasy, has written a far more popular version." Both limbs supported. Not VERBATIM: the supplied quote 'sounds like traditional Chinese wuxia' differs from the page ('sound like a traditional Chinese wuxia'), and the page hedges the judgement as Li Hong-man's ('may be').

verdicts.trueWording: "fer que els orcs tinguessin un parlar com més desballestat millor"
verdicts.note: PDF fetched from ddd.uab.cat and text-extracted with pdfminer (17pp). Quote present verbatim. Limb 1: "Sabia, això sí, que el llibre es publicaria en una col·lecció escolar... Per això, prou curiosament, El hòbbit és més farcit de cultismes o formes potser un xic arcaiques o desuetes que no pas d'altres traduccions." Limb 2: "els únics detalls lingüístics... van ser alguns trets peculiars emprats pels homes del sud (Bóromir, Fàramir…): aqueix, son/seua, naltros, mos/vos..." Limb 3 is the quoted orc clause. All three limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: "el cas de les dues traduccions alemanyes existents és invers"
verdicts.note: Same PDF. Page: "Segons que sembla, el cas de les dues traduccions alemanyes existents és invers: la primera, de Margaret Carroux, publicada entre 1969 i 1970, gaudeix de més «prestigi» que no pas la segona, de l'any 2000..." The immediately preceding section is the Swedish case (Ohlmarks 1959-61 superseded by the orthodox Andersson/Olsson 2005), so 'invers' does refer to the Swedish. No quote was supplied, hence SUBSTANCE not VERBATIM; the page hedges with 'Segons que sembla' (apparently).

verdicts.trueWording: "adding words and indulging in lengthy paraphrases... more complicated and high-faluting"
verdicts.note: Raw wikitext of en.wikipedia Translation_of_The_Lord_of_the_Rings_into_Swedish. 'high-faluting' appears verbatim in the Strömbom footnote translation: "by embroidering Tolkien's text, adding words and indulging in lengthy paraphrases, by frankly stubbornly turning the simple language into a more complicated and high-faluting one". The 'hyperbolic' limb is supported separately on the same page: "Andreas Brunner commented... that Ohlmarks' prose is hyperbolic in style, where the original uses simple or even laconic language." All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: "he had intentionally created an interpretation of Tolkien, not a straight translation"
verdicts.note: Same page. Lead: "Ohlmarks rejected all criticism, stating that he had intentionally created an interpretation of Tolkien, not a straight translation." Quote is an exact substring. Refusal-of-revision limb: "He ignored complaints and calls for revision from readers" and "Ohlmarks remained impervious to the numerous complaints and calls for revision".

verdicts.trueWording: Sample table: Ohlmarks 42 words, Andersson and Olsson 24 words
verdicts.note: Same page, 'Prose' section. Strömbom's comparison table gives Tolkien 20 words, Ohlmarks 1959-1961 42 words, Andersson and Olsson 2005 24 words for 'Indeed, few Hobbits had ever seen or sailed upon the Sea...'. The laconic limb is supported: "Commentators including Petter Lindgren in Aftonbladet have remarked on Ohlmarks's wordy text compared to Andersson's more laconic version", and the page calls Tolkien's own language 'simple or even laconic'. No quote supplied, so SUBSTANCE; 'matched Tolkien's laconic tone' is the claim's phrasing, the page says only 'more laconic' than Ohlmarks.

verdicts.trueWording: "a readable, even and in large part correct translation"
verdicts.note: Same page. Henrik Williams in Dagens Nyheter: "Let me say that Andersson & Olsson have prepared a readable, even and in large part correct translation..." - quote is an exact substring. Second limb, Malte Persson in Göteborgsposten: "the new translation follows the original's fluent prose very closely, and only a linguistic pedant could find anything to object to". Both reviews are dated 27 September 2004 on the page although the article labels the version 2005.

verdicts.trueWording: Lavskägge = 'Lichenbeard'; beam-as-light is Quickbeam → Snabba solstrålen
verdicts.note: Same page. Two of three examples are supported: "Ohlmarks used Vattnadal ('Water-dale') for Rivendell, apparently, Tolkien commented, by way of taking riven for river"; and the names table gives Ford of Bruinen -> Björnavad ('Bear Ford'), "A guess, using English 'Bruin', a brown bear". The third is a conflation: the page glosses Lavskägge as 'Lichenbeard', Ohlmarks's rendering of Treebeard, while the beam-as-light misreading belongs to a different name entirely - "The Ent Quickbeam becomes Snabba solstrålen ('Swift Sunbeam'), apparently taking beam in the sense of 'beam of light' instead of 'tree'".

verdicts.trueWording: "Dr. Ohlmarks is a conceited person, less competent than charming Max Schuchart"
verdicts.note: Same page. Letter 263 blockquote: "The enclosure that you brought from Almqvist &c. was both puzzling and irritating. A letter in Swedish from fil. dr. Åke Ohlmarks, and a huge list (9 pages foolscap) of names in the L.R. which he had altered... the impression remains, nonetheless, that Dr. Ohlmarks is a conceited person..." - covers the nine-page altered-name list and 'both puzzling and irritating'. The Dutch limb is supported by the running text: "He thought Ohlmarks's version was even worse than Schuchart's 1956-57 Dutch translation". All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: his Vidstige "even outdoes the original's Strider"
verdicts.note: Same page: "Stefan Spjut, reviewing the new translation in Svenska Dagbladet, commented that Ohlmarks's version had its merits, and that his Vidstige 'even outdoes the original's Strider', but that people would probably get used to the new version." Word for word; the page uses a curly apostrophe in original's where the supplied quote uses an ASCII one - a typographic difference only. 'One reviewer conceded' matches Spjut allowing merits to a version he is otherwise superseding.

verdicts.trueWording: "prompting him to compile his Guide to the Names"; 1982 book, hostility from late 1970s
verdicts.note: Raw wikitext of en.wikipedia %C3%85ke_Ohlmarks. "Ohlmarks translation of Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings was strongly disliked by the author, prompting him to compile his 'Guide to the Names in The Lord of the Rings'." And: "As a result of the severe criticism... Ohlmarks in the late 1970s began to display hostility towards the 'Tolkien phenomenon', and in 1982 published a book titled Tolkien and Black Magic" (Tolkien och den svarta magin, 1982). Both limbs supported; no quote was supplied, hence SUBSTANCE.

verdicts.trueWording: "lade till adjektiv och piffade upp dialogen... en helt annan bok"
verdicts.note: Raw wikitext of sv.wikipedia %C3%96vers%C3%A4ttning_av_Sagan_om_ringen_till_svenska. "I Sydsvenska Dagbladet (2004) ger Andreas Brunner försiktig beröm: 'Tolkien ville få fram en ålderdomlig känsla med ett avskalat språk. Ohlmarks gjorde precis tvärtom, lade till adjektiv och piffade upp dialogen. Resultatet blev en förtjusande bok, men också en helt annan bok än den Tolkien hade skrivit'." Added adjectives, spruced-up dialogue, delightful but quite different book - all three limbs supported; no quote supplied, so SUBSTANCE.

verdicts.trueWording: "six meals a day" blev "sex vällagade måltider om dagen"
verdicts.note: Same sv.wikipedia page. "Leif Jacobsen har granskat Ohlmarks översättning... Dessutom menar han att översättaren genomgående broderar ut texten och lägger till information som inte finns i originalet. Exempel som han lyfter fram är 'six meals a day' som i Ohlmarks översättning blev 'sex vällagade måltider om dagen'." Quote present verbatim; the padding limb and the attribution to Jacobsen are both supported.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: to make the world feel ancient
verdicts.trueWording: "en levande sagovärld" with as little to do with England as possible
verdicts.note: Same sv.wikipedia page. Supported: "I Ohlmarks bok Tolkiens arv uppger denne att den egna uppgiften varit att göra en tolkning av Tolkien" (Tolkiens arv is 1978 in the page's source list), and the block quote "Jag gjorde först en noggrann slätöversättning av hela boken och skrev sedan radikalt om den, hela tiden ledd av en strävan att söka skildra en levande sagovärld som hade precis så lite att göra med England och engelskan som Tolkien tydligen avsett." The plain-draft-then-rewrite limb and the distance-from-England limb are exact. The 'feel ancient' limb is not in Ohlmarks's stated aim - he says a LIVING saga-world ('levande sagovärld'); the only 'ålderdomlig känsla' (archaic feeling) on the page is Brunner's description of what TOLKIEN wanted, of which he says Ohlmarks did the opposite.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: attributing the Merry death-blow and the two Prancing Pony names to Malte Persson
verdicts.trueWording: Persson: "missförstånd, felsyftningar, inkonsekvenser och godtyckliga tillägg"
verdicts.note: Same sv.wikipedia page. The first half is verbatim from Persson (Göteborgs-Posten, 2004): "Den är så späckad med missförstånd, felsyftningar, inkonsekvenser och godtyckliga tillägg..." Both examples exist on the page but neither is credited to Persson: the Witch-king error is unattributed article text in its own section ('Häxmästarens död' - "I de flesta upplagor… är det felaktigt hoben Meriadoc som ger Häxmästaren av Angmar det dödande hugget, medan det i själva verket är Éowyn"), and the inn's two names ('Den dansande ponnyn' in the prologue vs 'Den stegrande ponnyn' in the text) is sourced to Jacobsen and to the book itself. The 'including' limb therefore misattributes.
